Framing mismatch: the concept is framed predominantly as a scientific/technological research project (crop water-stress forecasting, model transferability, decision value), whereas MSCA-PF expected outcomes EO-03, EO-04, EO-05, EO-06 and EO-08 are framed around the fellow's networking/communication development and participating-organisation capacity (working conditions, training/supervision quality, attractiveness, feedback into teaching). These outcomes lack a direct project mechanism in the current concept and are only Assumed. The concept addresses the research subject but not the fellow-development / institutional framing of these outcomes.

strategic_differentiation: FIELDWISE's differentiation, drawn from strategic_positioning.md (§1.1.9 ¶102-110; §2.3 ¶239-249), is a deliberate shift of agricultural AI away from retrospective accuracy (R², RMSE, F1) toward prospective, transferable, decision-oriented predictive intelligence. It is defined by six transitions — spectral proxy→physiological target, hyperspectral discovery→satellite scaling, static detection→prospective prediction, internal validation→temporal transferability, single-country modelling→geographic transferability, and research accuracy→commercial-field decision value — operationalised through a staged validation ladder (MATE scientific development/validation → MVCRI cross-country transferability in Bulgaria → AgroVIR farmer-field operational transferability → DrR Web MVP research-to-operation delivery) and a novel Field Decision Value (FDV) evaluation layer. It builds on an existing DrR – Digital Agronomist prototype and explicitly responds to prior-evaluation criticisms on heterogeneous data treatment, economic/IP route-to-user, and late/fragmented milestones, distinguishing the proposal from accuracy-centred agricultural ML that is not tested for cross-season, cross-country or research-to-commercial transferability.
